subject: After-action brief: ClearPath inference availability event — summary & verification request
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <tom.benson@clearpath.io>, Emily Wu <emily.wu@clearpath.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: After-action brief: ClearPath inference availability event — summary & verification request

Hi Tom / Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time to speak with us earlier. Attached is our consolidated after-action brief for the availability disruption you observed on 2026-09-10 between 02:10–02:37 UTC. The package includes: a concise RCA, a minute-by-minute timeline (CSV), and a proposed remediation/verification plan with owners and dates.

Executive summary (top of the PDF):
- What happened: a regression in KV cache invalidation logic triggered a cascading increase in memory pressure for a subset of inference routers, which caused transient eviction spikes and connection churn under burst traffic.
- Impact: intermittent 502/504s for ~27 minutes for requests routed to the affected pool; no data exfiltration or PII exposure identified.
- Immediate mitigations applied: failover to warm standby pool, temporary throttling for high-concurrency clients, and a hotfix to avoid the eviction path.

What we need from you:
1) Confirm receipt of the attached package and whether ClearPath would like a redacted public-facing summary for your compliance records.
2) Please confirm whether the SOC2 evidence link below (we also attached the tech excerpt) satisfies your audit intake, or if you need additional artifacts.
3) Accept or propose adjustments to the verification window (we've suggested 14 days) so we can close the loop on the mitigations and record verification results.

Attachments: clearpath-rca-summary-20260912.pdf; event-timeline-20260912.csv; action-owners-commitments-20260912.xlsx
Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/clearpath/rca-2026-09-12

Short answers to likely questions are in the PDF; full technical appendices are available on request. I'll follow up with a targeted reply addressing the log-and-keys questions you raised.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference platform

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the package. A couple quick clarifications before we route this to our internal audit team: 

1) Were any customer encryption keys or credentials present in the KV cache at the time of the evictions? We need explicit confirmation for our security team.
2) The timeline notes a failover to a "warm standby pool" — can you confirm whether sessions were re-established seamlessly for in-flight requests or whether retries were required client-side?

If you can add a short paragraph addressing those two points I can share the brief with procurement and compliance today. Appreciate the thoroughness.

-Tom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: After-action brief: ClearPath inference availability event — summary & verification request

Rishi — forwarding Tom's two questions; drafting a concise technical response for the customer below.

Quoted text:
> On Sat, 12 Sep 2026 at 13:02 Tom Benson <tom.benson@clearpath.io> wrote:
> 
> Rishi —
> 
> Thanks for the quick turnaround and the package. A couple quick clarifications before we route this to our internal audit team: 
> 
> 1) Were any customer encryption keys or credentials present in the KV cache at the time of the evictions? We need explicit confirmation for our security team.
> 2) The timeline notes a failover to a "warm standby pool" — can you confirm whether sessions were re-established seamlessly for in-flight requests or whether retries were required client-side?

Neha's draft answer (for your review):

- Encryption keys/credentials: No. Our KV cache stores model context and tokenization metadata only for the affected router pool. Customer encryption keys and long-term credentials are never cached in plaintext. Key material is exclusively handled by the KMS integration (HSM-backed) and only transient references (non-reversible handles) are stored. We've scanned the in-memory snapshots from affected hosts; we found no handles that would enable credential reconstruction. We'll attach the memory-scrub verification logs to the Drive folder.

- Failover behavior: The warm-standby pool accepted new connections immediately once the router health check failed. For in-flight requests that were mid-response, many completed successfully after retry logic at the SDK layer; some client-side retries were required for a small subset (approx 0.7% of affected requests) and are flagged in the timeline CSV. Our hotfix removes the eviction path that caused the cascade and we've instrumented additional metrics to detect recurrence.

If that reads clean, I'll send to Tom and Emily with the attachments.

-Neha

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <tom.benson@clearpath.io>, Emily Wu <emily.wu@clearpath.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: After-action brief: ClearPath inference availability event — summary & verification request

Tom / Emily —

Thanks for the questions. Neha's draft below is accurate; I've pasted the short, customer-facing statements here for clarity and attached the same artifacts to this message.

1) Were any customer encryption keys or credentials present in the KV cache at the time of the evictions?
Short answer: No.
Details (summary): Our KV cache is purpose-built for model context (token IDs, short-lived decoding state). Customer encryption keys are stored and used solely via our KMS/HSM integration and are never written to application memory as reconstructable plaintext. We performed memory snapshot checks on all affected hosts and scanned for any key handles; none usable for credential reconstruction were found. Artifact: "memory-snapshots-scan-20260912.log" uploaded to the Drive folder.

2) Failover behavior for in-flight requests
Short answer: Warm-standby absorbed new connections immediately; ~0.7% of in-flight requests required client-side retry.
Details (summary): Health checks detected the router degradation and routed new traffic away within ~9s of the first error spike. In-flight requests behaved variably based on SDK retry settings — most completed after a single automatic retry; a small fraction experienced timeouts and needed an additional attempt. We've flagged those request ids in the timeline CSV and will coordinate with your engineers if you want a per-request export for forensic validation.

Next steps and commitments (owners & dates):
- 2026-09-16: Roll out a defensive config to limit simultaneous eviction activity (owner: Hannah Schmitt).
- 2026-09-20: Publish an SDK patch with improved client-side backoff defaults and telemetry (owner: Monica Patel).
- 2026-09-26: Post-verification report summarizing 14-day verification window and metrics (owner: Rishi Malhotra).

We understand the impact this had on your operations and will support whatever validation or evidence you need for your compliance/audit intake. Please reply with whether the 14-day verification window works for you or if you prefer a different window.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
